::: {.callout-important title="The association is descriptive and exploratory"}
The sign–speech association $\psi$ informs estimated total expressive vocabulary, including the overlap between speaking and signing. Four sources supply per-word categories for signs or gestures, speech and both: `uk_02`, `uk_07`, `es_01` and `nz_01` (@sec-speech-sign-association). The first three classify words within comprehension; the New Zealand source classifies produced words. The model uses their distinct likelihoods. An association above independence describes overlap under the model. It does not show that signing causes, speeds or delays speech.

**Study differences need careful interpretation.** The study-specific $\psi$ estimates are the main summaries. The population parameter is a pooled centre, rather than agreement among the sources. Earlier fits placed the Spanish estimate closer to independence than the UK and New Zealand estimates. The reason remains unresolved. The Spanish source includes spontaneous symbolic gestures and taught signs, while the other sources do not define their signing columns. Its authors also restricted gesture analysis to ten of 21 categories; whether the supplied totals include that restriction remains unconfirmed. Teaching differences are another possibility, but the sources do not record them. These counts cannot separate those explanations. A dated age-varying analysis found no clear added age effect after accounting for study. It did not establish that the association is constant in age. With four informing sources, the study spread remains sensitive to the prior.

**Signing coverage thins with age.** Signed observations are dense from about 12 to 60 months and sparse beyond: two small sources above 72 months and one above 84, so older-age estimates depend more on the assumed smooth trajectory. Both $r(a)$ and $p_{\text{any}}$ are reported only within the comprehension-conditioned age cap. The peak age of $r(a)$ is estimated, but under a fixed three-anchor shape whose outer reference ages are asserted rather than fitted, and the signed GP's length-scale is not identified, so the signed trajectory remains substantially parametric in practice. The registered signing models describe children with Down syndrome; there is no registered TD signing model.

**Recovery checks limit how confidently the association can be reported.** The early checks found downward error in some population and study-specific association estimates. Later reporting-quality checks reduced that concern and showed why unconverged recovery fits must not be scored. These few replicates do not establish the direction or size of bias for every source. Read the per-study intervals, the prior-sensitivity results and the converged recovery evidence together. Neither crossing the independence reference nor a positive point estimate establishes a causal effect. See the [reporting-quality recovery record](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth/blob/main/notes/202609031825-recovery-vg15-vg12-vg11.md).

:::
